annotations.rfc_basis: RFC 2045 section 5.2: a part with no Content-Type header has the default text/plain; charset=us-ascii. So this part is a text/plain body view exactly as a twin that declares 'text/plain; charset=us-ascii' would be, and the quote stage must read it: the attribution and its '>' block are the same on_wrote_en boundary the explicit twin gets.
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was typed by a model from the RFC rule (RFC 2045 section 5.2, the default text/plain) and read out of the fixture bytes (a byte/offset listing); never produced by running the library. The quote span and per-line prefix depths are the design's span conventions (a run to the end of the part keeps its final terminator; an attribution carries the contiguous block that follows it). labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person.
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, part.tree, part.gaps, decode.chain and body.content_sha256 -- what the skeleton walker measures today (it records content_type null, never an invented default, and its charset ladder runs the default us-ascii).
annotations.phase_1_facts: document.axes, body.text, body.quote_boundaries, body.view_levels and body.selection; the quote facts are the point of the fixture.
annotations.not_yet_labelled: headers.fields, part.regions and body.preamble_epilogue are not typed here: this turn fixates on the effective media type and labels the phase-1 facts the RFC fixes. statuses (phase 2), thread edges and TimeEvents (phase 3) are not exercised.
